_about: Invented material for --demo. Every organisation, person, paper and URL here is fictional and every link points at example.com. Nothing in this file is a real claim about anyone.

items.title: Northwind Systems opens its evaluation harness
items.summary: Fictional vendor Northwind Systems released the test harness it uses internally, including 4,000 graded failure cases.

items.title: Regulators publish draft disclosure rules for automated decisions
items.summary: A fictional draft rule would require organisations to disclose when an automated system materially affects a customer decision.

items.title: Meridian Labs reports a 40 percent drop in serving cost
items.summary: Fictional company Meridian Labs attributes the drop to batching changes rather than new hardware.

papers.title: Measuring silent failure in retrieval-augmented pipelines
papers.whats_new: A fictional benchmark showing retrieval pipelines return confident answers from empty result sets in 12 percent of queries.
papers.why_it_matters: Worth checking whether your own pipeline distinguishes no results from bad results.

papers.title: Cost-aware routing between model tiers
papers.whats_new: A fictional routing method that sends only uncertain queries to the larger model, holding accuracy within one point.
papers.why_it_matters: The savings come from measuring uncertainty well, which is the part most teams skip.

papers.title: What evaluation sets forget after six months
papers.whats_new: A fictional longitudinal study finding fixed evaluation sets stop predicting production quality after roughly two quarters.
papers.why_it_matters: An argument for rotating held-out cases on a schedule rather than freezing a benchmark.

federal.title: Draft rule on automated decision disclosure
federal.text: Fictional draft text. Comment period runs 60 days. Applies to organisations above a size threshold.

global.title: Cross-border guidance on model documentation
global.text: Fictional guidance harmonising documentation expectations across three example jurisdictions.

debates.topic: Whether open evaluation harnesses help or leak

positions.summary: Publishing the harness is the only way outside reviewers can reproduce a vendor's claims.
An open harness becomes a target: teams tune to the test and the number stops meaning anything.

debates.takeaway: Both are right about different time horizons, which is why the release date of a benchmark matters as much as its contents.
